frontier_paragraphs: **Question:** Can we sample an ordered list of transpositions with product identity, nearly uniformly over all such lists of the prescribed length, in time polynomial in permutation degree N and output length m? Any algorithm is allowed; fast mixing of a particular walk is a separate goal.

**Current answer:** Global near-uniform samplers survive in short, sparse and sufficiently long regimes; no all-length theorem is established. The consolidated campaigns add exact connected genus-two constructions and a uniform exact connected sampler with cost A C^(g+1)(N+g+2)^15. This is polynomial at logarithmic genus but does not close the global intermediate-length gap. An exact sparse global candidate has unfinished review and remains provisional.

**Two different frontiers:** Connected words can now be sampled at every genus with exponential genus cost. The global question is whether that cost can be paid under the exact component law, or replaced by a uniform polynomial bound. The local {3,4,5} heat-bath mixing question is separate and remains open; direct sampling proves no gap for that walk.

**Evidence level:** Campaign results are documentary imports of exact statements and scoped internal verdicts, not fresh mathematical certification. Same-model reviews are correlated. Initial provisional banners are retained alongside later exact reconciliations. The older October author records keep their provisional scope; the large heat-bath archive remains only partly traced. Interrupted sparse-sampler reviews are not accepted by this consolidation.

**Conventions:** Products act rightmost first. The core word models are labeled and ordered; auxiliary graph models are declared separately. Time is polynomial in N and m, not log N wires. Odd identity length is infeasible; m=0 is the empty word; m=2 is a uniform doubled transposition; N=2 has one word at each even length. For a connected identity component on v labels, ell=2v-2+2g defines its nonnegative genus g, a measure of length beyond the minimum.

**Graph-directed macro distinction:** HB-NONLOCAL-LIFT gives constructive all-endpoint pair-chain connectivity and a polynomial gap comparison, leaving general mixing open. HB-TREE-MACRO gives a separate fast completed-sequence sampler for minimal full-cycle words by decoding tree slides; it does not bound ordinary adjacent Hurwitz mixing.

**Ideas for future agents (2026-11-06):** [Four research questions](notes/research-questions-2026-11-06.md) formulate gate-library representation balance, Toffoli connectivity, local transposition surgery/proofs of equivalence, and a hidden planted identity-subsequence assumption. These are proposed questions only; no investigation or new mathematical acceptance is implied.

Surviving Samplers.text: Exact short bridges: polynomial for m <= A(log N)^2, with fixed A; the full algorithm has exp(O(sqrt(min(m,N)))) state growth.

Dense bridges: put q=floor(m/[2N(N-1)]). For q>=4ceil(log2 N), TV <= min(1,3N^2 exp(-q/144)). Fixed-constant N^2 log N lengths give only inverse-polynomial error from this bound; q/log N -> infinity suffices for negligible error.
Sparse bridges: negligible error for even m <= N^(2/3) ln N / 4, with explicit but very large asymptotic onset. The earlier theorem keeps a better error bound on its smaller range.
Exact connected genus-zero/one components remain useful primitives; later S-G2 and S-GENUS-FPT extend their genus coverage.
Exact small-support components of any genus: a quotient-state decoder reaches support size proportional to log(N+m), capped at N.
Connected genus-two arbitrary-endpoint sampling is exact, with conservative expected O(v^11 log^3(v+1)) bit time; a separate cut construction handles identity genus two.
One exact connected sampler handles every genus with expected A C^(g+1)(N+g+2)^15 bit time. For each fixed K, g<=K log(N+2) is polynomial-time. This is not a global all-length theorem.

What Failed.text: The current small-component/low-genus policies lose almost all target mass on an explicit m=N^(3/4) subsequence. Enlarging only the polynomial quotient cutoff does not repair this.
Low-genus-only output is not a general solution: even exact genus-one components cover a vanishing fraction at m=2N.
Uniform Hurwitz randomization cannot choose the correct global orbit weights.
Polynomial scalar counts do not automatically give a decoder for literal words, and several insertion/support shortcuts have explicit counterexamples.
The low-genus/small-support eligibility obstruction persists even when the allowed genus grows through N^(1/8), on the stated m=N^(3/4) subsequence. This does not prove general sampling hardness.

Precise Gaps.text: Exact macro assembly is available. The connected primitive's exponential genus dependence must be removed or paid in expectation to obtain a global theorem in new regimes; the stronger uniform-polynomial sufficient condition remains open.
No all-length sampler is established, and no general hardness theorem explains the uncovered range.
The local heat-bath chain still needs an inverse-polynomial full-chain gap. Several auxiliary routes and counterexamples narrow methods without resolving this.

Other Generator Families.text: For (S3)^k with literal within-triple transpositions, a new self-contained Hurwitz/square-refresh proof gives gap >=1/(200 k m^12). Counts vary; fixed triple partition. Author result with exact checks, provisionally registered pending independent review.

Endpoint Walk Benchmarks.text: For minimal factorizations of one full cycle, square refresh never acts and the Hurwitz kernel is comparable to two-factor heat bath. A separate Prüfer-coordinate walk mixes rapidly; polynomial mixing of the adjacent walk remains unresolved here.

For full-cycle length N+1, the original pair hybrid remains open at growing N. S3 all-length mixing, a balanced-square branch improvement and a frozen exact-multigraph obstruction are proved in a new author report.

A separate tree-plus-2h-extra-edges global refresh has an exact spanning-tree rejection correction. Its hybrid mixes in O_h(N^h log(1/epsilon)) completed attempts at fixed h, including explicit N+1 and N+3 bounds; it does not prove pair-slide mixing.

For the actual adjacent K_A, a uniform-in-N length-three gap >=1/24 yields constant-factor comparison with exact triple heat bath at every length. A local correlation obstruction prevents the tested proof from extending to the full-cycle N+1 polynomial gap.

The actual arbitrary-position pair walk has gap between 1/(2m) and 3/(4m) in S3. For every N its Dirichlet form lies between (2/m) and 4m^2 times the adjacent form; growing-N full-cycle mixing remains unresolved.

The support marginal has compatible-order weights, but the actual all-pair walk does not close on support graphs, even for full-cycle N+1. Its averaged graph kernel does not describe the observed process beyond one step; polynomial growing-N marginal mixing remains unresolved.

Independent ternary Hurwitz matching updates have layer gap between (1/48)min(m gamma,1) and (m/2)gamma on each orbit; nonidentity endpoints require a twisted seam. This gives a parallel speedup and a commuting benchmark, while growing-N full-cycle mixing remains unresolved.

Auxiliary Graph Walks.text: With circuit order and functionality discarded, labeled-tree edge slides have gap >=2/[(N-1)^2(N-2)^2], for both the natural wedge-weighted target and a uniform-tree correction. Author comparison proof, provisionally registered; no transfer to adjacent Hurwitz mixing.

Pending Review.text: An exact sparse global candidate has a completed conditional theory review and successful finite production checks, but blind/implementation review and final reconciliation are unfinished. Do not cite it as accepted.
Foreground projection and replacement-endpoint identities are preserved with exact checks; an independent proof audit is still needed. Endpoint agreement alone gives no word-level pseudorandomness.

Cryptographic Investigations.text: Sparse replacements fail to hide the two specified relator/path-star constructions: short-relation and support tests give efficient distinguishers. The general noisy-word hiding question remains open.

policy_definitions: All direct samplers below use independent fair bits in their mathematical model; seeded finite PRNG tests are reproducibility checks, not a proof of exact randomness.

Let P=N+m+2 and K=max{1<=v<=N: v^(2v)<=P^4}, fixed at the original top-level input. H0 permits every component with g<=1 OR v<=K. H1 permits only v<=K. Isolates have size 1, length 0; both policies permit arbitrary genus on small supports.

H2 permits every component of size at most L=max{1<=v<=N:3^v<=P^4}. Each policy has an exact uniform law on its own allowed subset, not automatically on all Omega. Global TV is exactly the omitted count fraction, 1-Z_allowed/Z.
These cutoffs are fixed by the original (N,m), never silently recomputed after deleting components. Polynomial state counts can coexist with an allowed subset of vanishing global mass.
For arbitrary all-transposition endpoints (N>=2), feasibility is m>=N-cycles(sigma) with matching parity. The star-generator model has its own feasibility criterion, not this one.
